The longest-serving chief minister in his Indian state's history, this politician co-founded a socialist party in 1994 alongside George Fernandes — who is he?
Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists: Political organization. The OUN was mostly active preceding, during, and immediately after the Second World War.

Beginning with the rise of Augustus in 27 BC and ending with the death of Marcus Aurelius in 180 AD, this roughly 200-year golden age saw the empire reach its greatest territorial extent under Trajan — what was it?
Pax Romana: Roman golden age (27 BC to 180). It was during this period that the Roman Empire achieved its greatest territorial extent under Trajan in 117.
The fifth governor of Roman Judaea under Tiberius, he presided over the trial of Jesus — and is so central to Christianity that he's named in both the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds; who is he?
Pontius Pilate: Roman governor of Judea and condemner of Jesus.
The favorite of Jacob's two wives and mother of Joseph and Benjamin, her older sister Leah was Jacob's first wife — who is she?
In 1682 this French explorer canoed the lower Mississippi to the Gulf and claimed its whole basin for France, naming it La Louisiane after Louis XIV. Who was he?
René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle
Jean-François de Galaup, comte de Lapérouse
René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle: French explorer of North America (1643–1687)
René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle

This December 1989 uprising began in the city of Timișoara and ended with the swift trial and execution of a longtime Communist dictator and his wife — which nation's uprising, the only one of 1989 to end that way?
Romanian revolution: 1989 popular uprising in Romania.
Nicknamed "Sam Bahadur" — the Brave — and a Military Cross winner in WWII, he led India's army during the 1971 war with Pakistan and became the country's first field marshal. Which general was he?
Known as 'the eye of Ra,' this Egyptian warrior goddess of medicine is often linked with Hathor and Bastet — who is she?
Sekhmet: Ancient Egyptian goddess. Sekhmet is also a solar deity, sometimes given the epithet "the eye of Ra".
Born in Singapore in 1983, this former Xiaomi finance chief has run a wildly popular ByteDance-owned video app since 2021 — who is he?
Shou Zi Chew: Singaporean business executive (born 1983)
A barrister who founded his own Democratic Party, this politician stepped up after Makarios III's death to lead his Mediterranean island nation as president from 1977 to 1988 — who was he?
Spyros Kyprianou: President of Cyprus from 1977 to 1988.
Led by Alexis Tsipras, who twice served as Greece's prime minister starting in 2015, this pro-European left-wing coalition was founded in 2004 — which party?
Syriza: Political party in Greece. It was founded in 2004 as a political coalition of left-wing and radical left parties, and registered as a political party in 2012.
Known as 'the Great,' this Roman emperor was the last to rule the entire empire single-handedly and helped enshrine the Nicene Creed as orthodox doctrine — who was he?
Theodosius I: Roman emperor from 379 to 395.
According to Catholic teaching, this change during the eucharistic prayer turns bread and wine into the Body and Blood of Christ while their outward appearance stays the same — what is it called?

Sparked by a suppressed student demonstration in Prague on International Students' Day in November 1989, this peaceful transfer of power ended 41 years of one-party rule in Czechoslovakia — what was it called?
Velvet Revolution: Democratization process in Czechoslovakia in 1989.
After rising through China's banking sector to become mayor of Beijing, this retired official later led the Communist Party's anti-corruption watchdog from 2012 to 2017 — who is he?
Wang Qishan: Vice President of China from 2018 to 2023.
Known as "Bill," this British field marshal led the so-called "forgotten army" in the Burma campaign before later serving as governor-general of Australia — who was he?
William Slim, 1st Viscount Slim: British Army field marshal, Governor-General of Australia, and author (1891–1970)

This Israeli politician served as defense minister from 2022 until his dismissal by the prime minister in November 2024, having earlier held posts including construction, immigration, and education minister after starting out in the navy. Who is he?
Yoav Gallant: Israeli politician & military officer (born 1958)
Who wrote The Emperor's New Clothes?

The Emperor's New Clothes → Hans Christian Andersen. The tale has been translated into over 100 languages.
"The Emperor's New Clothes" was first published with "The Little Mermaid" in Copenhagen, Denmark, by C.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Assembly language (founded 1949) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Dmitri Mendeleev is a chemist. The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
What is the atomic number of Flerovium?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
What is the atomic number of Yttrium?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
In what year was Galileo Galilei born?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Anton Chekhov born?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Max Weber born?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year did Gregor Mendel die?
Gregor Mendel: Mendel worked with seven characteristics of pea plants: plant height, pod shape and colour, seed shape and colour, and flower position and colour.
In what year did Adam Smith die?
Adam Smith: The work is notable for its contribution to economic theory, particularly in its exposition of the concept of absolute advantage.
In what year was Argon discovered?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Which company manufactures Consolidated B-24 Liberator?
Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control
Consolidated B-24 Liberator: North American Aviation. The Consolidated B-24 Liberator is an American heavy bomber, designed by Consolidated Aircraft of San Diego, California.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Circinus?
Circinus: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
Who is credited with discovering Citric acid?
Citric acid: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
Who is credited with discovering Helium?
Helium: Pierre Janssen. Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Russell Crowe stars in this 2001 Ron Howard film about a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician's struggle with schizophrenia, based on Sylvia Nasar's biography. What's the title?
A Beautiful Mind (film) is a 2001 American biographical drama film about the mathematician John Nash who won a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
This French surgeon won the 1912 Nobel for pioneering vascular suturing, then teamed up with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build the first perfusion pump for organ transplantation. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel (28 June 1873 - 5 November 1944) was a French surgeon and biologist who spent most of his scientific career in the United States.
Multicellular, oxygen-breathing, and all descended from a single common ancestor, this kingdom ranges in size from 8.5 micrometers to 33.6 meters. What is it?
Animal are multicellular, eukaryotic organisms belonging to the biological kingdom Animalia.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Found in almost every habitat except the open sea and the poles, the order Coleoptera is the largest of all and accounts for about a quarter of every known animal species — which insects are these?
Beetle are insects that form the order Coleoptera, in the superorder Holometabola.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
This large, stocky black corvid fills a niche across Eurasia comparable to a similar bird found in North America, but is bigger and huskier than its transatlantic counterpart — what species is it?
Carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Defined by a hollow dorsal nerve cord, an endostyle, and a post-anal tail at some point in life, this phylum spans vertebrates, tunicates, and lancelets alike — which option fits?
Chordate is a bilaterian animal belonging to the phylum Chordata (kor-).
This towering annual in the daisy family yields seeds in two flavors — oilseed (the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil) and the confectionary kind you crack as a snack — which plant?
Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae.
This bluish-purple discoloration of the skin, most visible on the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes, signals a drop in oxygen bound to hemoglobin in the blood — name the condition?
Cyanosis is the change of tissue color to a bluish-purple hue, as a result of decrease in the amount of oxygen bound to the hemoglobin in the red blood cells of the capillary bed.
Sucrose, lactose, and maltose are the best-known examples of this water-soluble carbohydrate class, each formed by linking two simple sugars together — what's the term?
Disaccharide (also called a double sugar or biose) is the sugar formed when two monosaccharides are joined by glycosidic linkage.
Once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil, these true seals of the genus Mirounga are named for the male's large trunk-like snout, with males weighing up to 4,000 kilograms — which animal?
Elephant seal are very large, oceangoing true seals in the genus Mirounga.
Aerobic exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all induce this intense feeling of well-being — which is also, less happily, a symptom of mania — what state is it?
Euphoria (yoo-) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
This omnivorous insect, common in North American homes, gets its name from ear-shaped hindwings and carries pincers on its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia is a species complex comprising the common earwig.
Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater has a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth and a pot-shaped bulb on the males' noses — what is it?
Gharial (Gavialis gangeticus), also known as gavial or fish-eating crocodile, is a crocodilian in the family Gavialidae and among the longest of all living crocodilians.

Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, this non-cancerous condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men and can occur in newborns, adolescents, and older or obese men — name the condition?

Gynecomastia (also spelled gynaecomastia) is the non-cancerous enlargement of one or both breasts in men due to the growth of breast tissue as a result of a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens.
With species ranging from evergreen trees to climbing shrubs across the tropics and temperate zones, this genus's most iconic species decorates Christmas cards worldwide — what genus is it?
Holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats pain, fever, and inflammation — from migraines to arthritis — and typically starts working within an hour, whether taken orally or intravenously. What drug?
Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is used to relieve pain, fever, and inflammation.

This American scientist co-authored a landmark 1953 paper with Francis Crick proposing the double-helix structure of DNA, building on research by Rosalind Franklin, and shared a 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery — who is he?
James Watson (April 6, 1928 - November 6, 2025) was an American molecular biologist, geneticist, and zoologist.
This Soviet-designed naval helicopter has spawned variants for assault transport, export, and civilian use, and still flies today from Russia to India -- which aircraft?

Kamov Ka-27 (NATO reporting name 'Helix') is a military helicopter developed for the Soviet Navy, and as of 2024 is in service in various countries including Russia, Ukraine, Vietnam, China, South Korea, and India.

Seen using a silver stain and grown on media containing the amino acid cysteine, this genus of bacteria causes a severe pneumonia-like illness as well as a milder flu-like illness called Pontiac fever — name the genus?
Legionella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria that can be seen using a silver stain or grown in a special media that contains cysteine, an amino acid.

Ranging across Eurasia with plumage of black, white, pink, and grey, this small insectivorous bird forms compact family flocks of six to seventeen outside the breeding season, its northern subspecies sporting all-white heads — which bird?
Long-tailed tit (Aegithalos caudatus) is a common bird species belonging to the bushtit family found throughout Eurasia.

Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" elsewhere, these burrow-dwelling marine crustaceans are among the top predators of tropical shallows — yet they remain poorly understood. What are they?
Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek (stma) 'mouth' and (pos) 'foot').
Used to treat cancers, autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, and even ectopic pregnancies, this chemotherapy drug and immune suppressant can be taken either orally or by injection — name it?
Methotrexate is a chemotherapy agent and immune-system suppressant.
Sitting just above the lip and under the nose, this style of facial hair on men has come in countless shapes across the centuries — what's it called?
Moustache is a growth of facial hair grown above the upper lip and under the nose of men.
This form of vitamin B3 is taken orally to treat pellagra without the skin-flushing side effect of niacin, and used as a cream to fight acne and reduce signs of aging skin — what's the compound?
Nicotinamide (INN, BAN UK) or niacinamide (USAN US) (IUPAC name: 3-pyridinecarboxoamide) is a form of vitamin B3 found in food and used as a dietary supplement and medication.

These pouched mammals originated in South America and crossed into the north during the Great American Interchange; one species is so common in the U.S. that people just call it a 'possum.' What is it?
Opossum are members of the marsupial order Didelphimorphia endemic to the Americas.
He co-founded Microsoft with his childhood friend Bill Gates in 1975, then stepped back from daily work in 1983 after a lymphoma diagnosis and founded Vulcan Inc. with his sister — who was he?
Paul Allen (January 21, 1953 - October 15, 2018) was an American businessman, computer programmer, and investor.

First described in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the cellar spider and the "vibrating spider" — and lends the nickname "daddy long-legs" to one of its species; what is the family?
Pholcidae are a family of araneomorph spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Ancient Chinese philosopher Confucius believed this oratorical skill could profoundly move even those not present in the room — what is the term for addressing a live audience?
Public speaking is the delivery of a speech to a live audience.
Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flow,' this umbrella term covers more than 200 different conditions causing chronic joint or connective-tissue pain, including arthritis — what's the term?
Rheumatism (from the Ancient Greek, rhema) or rheumatic disorders are conditions causing chronic, often intermittent pain affecting the joints or connective tissue.
After dropping out of Stanford and co-founding a startup later sold for over $40 million, this entrepreneur led Y Combinator before taking the helm of a leading AI company — who is he?
Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019.

This dog breed from southern China, traditionally kept as a property guardian, was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century and is known in the West for its deep wrinkles. What breed is this?

Shar Pei (Cantonese; pinyin: sh p) is a dog breed from
southern China.
This family of roughly 1,450 moth species, with narrow wings and streamlined bodies built for fast, hovering flight, are so nimble they're routinely mistaken for hummingbirds — what are they called?
Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths, with many of their caterpillars known as hornworms.

Which British single-seat fighter plane, the only such aircraft Britain produced continuously throughout World War II, was famous for its innovative elliptical wing designed to be as thin as possible?
Supermarine Spitfire is a British single-seat fighter aircraft that was used by the Royal Air Force and other Allied countries before, during, and after World War II.
Used to treat asthma and COPD, this methylxanthine drug — a cousin of caffeine — turns up in trace amounts in tea, chocolate, and yerba mate. What is it?
Theophylline is a drug that inhibits phosphodiesterase and blocks adenosine receptors.
Named for the compulsive pulling of one's own hair, this disorder brings a brief positive feeling with each pull but is notoriously hard to stop — what is it?
Trichotillomania (TTM), also known as hair-pulling disorder or compulsive hair pulling, is a mental disorder characterized by a long-term urge that results in the pulling out of one's own hair.
This broad category of creative disciplines spans painting, sculpture, photography, and architecture, and includes applied fields like industrial and fashion design — what do we call it?
Visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
This mosquito-borne viral disease causes chills, nausea, and muscle pain, and in about 15% of cases progresses to liver damage that turns the skin a telltale color — what disease is it?
Yellow fever is a viral disease of typically short duration.
This class of bony fish accounts for nearly 99% of all living fish species, ranging in size from an 8-millimeter minnow to a giant sunfish weighing 2,700 kilograms — what is it?
Actinopterygii: Class of ray-finned bony fishes.
Its very name comes from the Arabic for 'the kohl,' and chemically it's any compound carrying a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon — a family that ranges from methanol to cholesterol. What is it?
Alcohol (chemistry): Organic compound with at least one hydroxyl (–OH) group.
This functional group, formed by replacing a carboxylic acid's hydroxyl with an amino group, creates the peptide bonds that link amino acids into proteins — what is it?
Amide: Organic compounds of the form RC(=O)NR′R″.
Belonging to the suborder Vermilingua and closely related to sloths, these mammals include giant, silky, and tamandua species that feed almost exclusively on ants and termites — what are they called?
Anteater: Mammals known for eating ants and termites.
Who is this — “German murderer and cannibal (born 1961)”?

Armin Meiwes: German murderer and cannibal (born 1961). After Meiwes and the victim jointly attempted to eat the victim's severed penis, Meiwes murdered his victim and proceeded to eat a large amount of his flesh.
Evolving from a troubled twin-engine predecessor into a four-engine heavy bomber powered by Rolls-Royce Merlin engines, which British WWII aircraft became one of the RAF's most famous bombers?
Avro Lancaster: World War II British heavy bomber aircraft.

When no one else had the staff for it, this American lawyer volunteered to prosecute the Einsatzgruppen trial at Nuremberg, then spent decades championing an International Criminal Court — who was he?
This insect order unites cockroaches with termites, after genetic evidence showed termites are actually evolved, eusocial cockroaches. What's the order called?
Blattodea: Order of insects that includes cockroaches and termites.
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Discovered in 1817 simultaneously by two German chemists as an impurity in zinc carbonate, this soft silvery-white metal shares chemical traits with zinc and mercury — which element?
Cadmium: Chemical element with atomic number 48 (Cd)
Called the 'father of modern taxonomy,' which Swedish biologist formalized the two-name system for naming living things and was later ennobled as von Linné?
Carl Linnaeus: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778)
First flown in 1955 as a tricycle-gear evolution of an earlier taildragger model, this four-seat high-wing aircraft is the most-produced plane in history — which model is it?
Cessna 172: Propeller driven single engine aircraft.

Most often documented in boxers and football players, this neurodegenerative disease is linked to repeated blows to the head and can worsen into dementia — what's its name, usually shortened to three letters?
Chronic traumatic encephalopathy: Neurodegenerative disease caused by head injury.
Thought extinct since the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this lobe-finned fish was found alive off the west Indian Ocean, more closely related to lungfish than typical fish — what is it?
This transparent structure at the front of the eye provides about two-thirds of its focusing power and can be reshaped with LASIK surgery — what is it?
Cornea: Transparent front layer of the eye. The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.
Native to South and Southeast Asia and often sold as fresh stems, this tropical plant known as West Indian lemon grass can't survive a frost — what is it?
A fluorinated glucocorticoid, this medication treats everything from severe allergies and asthma to brain swelling and croup, and is given to ease preterm-labor outcomes — what is it?
Dexamethasone: Corticosteroid medication. The effects of dexamethasone are frequently seen within a day and last for about three days.
Also called Trisomy 21, this condition is caused by an extra copy of a single chromosome and grows more likely with a mother's age — from under 0.1% at 20 to about 3% at 45. What is it?

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?

These small to medium passerine birds have stout conical bills for cracking seeds and nuts, a worldwide native range excluding Australia and the poles, and include canaries, siskins, and Darwin's famous Galápagos group — what bird family is this?
Finch: Family of birds. The true finches are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
This Austrian economist shared the 1974 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Gunnar Myrdal for his work on how prices communicate information — who is he?
Friedrich Hayek: Austrian economist and philosopher (1899–1992)

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)
This inflammatory arthritis brings on rapid, searing pain — often in the joint at the base of the big toe — caused by needle-shaped crystals of uric acid building up in the blood. What is it?
Gout: Form of arthritis causing swollen joints.
Its name literally combines words for 'holy' and 'flatfish,' reflecting its popularity on Catholic holy days — this demersal fish is prized both as food and as a sport catch. Which fish?
This field of study focuses on the methodological principles of interpreting texts — especially biblical and philosophical writings — and is closely related to exegesis. What is it called?
Hermeneutics: The study of the methodological principles of interpretation. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
In Greek myth, this fragrant spring bulb sprang from the blood of a youth slain by a jealous west wind god who coveted his bond with Apollo — what flower is it?
Roche once used up to 90% of the world's crop of this star-shaped spice to manufacture the flu drug Tamiflu via shikimic acid — what is it?
Illicium verum: Star anise, an evergreen tree.
The largest tree fruit on Earth can hit 120 pounds and 35 inches long — a 'multiple fruit' made of thousands of individual flowers, with a single tree bearing hundreds a year. What is it?
This physician ran the Battle Creek Sanitarium — part spa, part hospital, part luxury hotel — where he treated the rich and poor alike and devised numerous nut and vegetable products — who is it?
Born in Kabul to a diplomat, this Afghan-American physician-turned-novelist wrote the bestselling 'The Kite Runner' before serving as a UNHCR goodwill ambassador — who is he?
Khaled Hosseini: Afghan-American novelist (born 1965). Hosseini's novels have spread awareness about Afghanistan's people and culture.
This probability principle explains why a casino might lose money on a single spin of roulette but reliably earns a predictable percentage over many thousands of spins. What is it called?
Law of large numbers: Averages of repeated trials converge to the expected value.
Instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission, this Austrian-Swedish physicist fled Nazi Germany in 1938 after losing her post under the Nuremberg Laws — who is she?

Fired by IBM in 1968 for revealing her intent to transition — an apology that took until 2020 — this computer scientist had already invented dynamic instruction handling behind modern out-of-order execution. Who was she?
Lynn Conway: American computer scientist and electrical engineer (1938–2024)

Originally hoping to become an engineer, this Italian physician became one of the first women to graduate from medical school in Italy and later devised an influential educational philosophy — who is she?
Maria Montessori: Italian physician and educator (1870–1952)

Encompassing conditions marked by a clinically significant disturbance in thinking, emotional regulation, or behavior that causes real distress or impaired functioning, this broad psychiatric category has causes that remain often unclear — what is the umbrella term for it?
Nicknamed 'Foxbat' by NATO and built largely from stainless steel, this Soviet interceptor still holds the altitude record for an airbreathing piloted aircraft at 38 km — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25: Family of interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft.
Born in China and educated at MIT and Stanford, this billionaire engineer founded Taiwan's dominant chipmaker, serving as its CEO from 1987 to 2005 — who is he?
Morris Chang: Taiwanese businessman and electrical engineer (born 1931)

The males of this stocky Arctic cetacean sport a spiralled 'tusk' up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to work as a weapon, a tool, and maybe a salinity sensor. What animal is it?

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.

Born out of military planning before World War II, this branch of applied mathematics uses optimization and statistics to find the best possible outcome for real-world decisions — what field, sometimes called management science?
Operations research: Discipline concerning the application of advanced analytical methods.
Also called the corn poppy or Flanders poppy, this red flowering weed has symbolized remembrance in the Commonwealth since World War I — what plant is it?
Papaver rhoeas: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
Native to Asia, Europe, and western North America, this flowering shrub's fragrant blooms last just 7 to 10 days each spring — which plant?
Peony: Genus of flowering plants in the family Paeoniaceae.
Known across South Asia as Indian gooseberry or amla, this deciduous tree is native to tropical regions of the continent — which plant?
Phyllanthus emblica: Berry and plant. Phyllanthus emblica, commonly known as emblic, Indian gooseberry, amalaki, amloki, or amla, is a deciduous tree of the family Phyllanthaceae.
This birth defect results in one or more extra fingers or toes and has been linked to at least 39 different genetic mutations — what is it called?
Polydactyly: Physical anomaly involving extra fingers or toes.

Native to western Eurasia and a member of the rose family, this species — the wild or sweet cherry — is the ancestor of the sour cherry, though every part of the plant except its ripe fruit is mildly toxic. What is it called?
Prunus avium: Species of flowering plant in the rose family. The species is often cultivated as an ornamental tree.
Also known as hexogen, this nitroamine explosive is the key energetic agent in C-4 and a core ingredient of Semtex — which compound?
RDX: Explosive chemical compound. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.

Covering more than 200 conditions from arthritis to soft-tissue pain syndromes, this umbrella term for chronic joint and connective-tissue pain gives its name to a whole medical specialty — what is it called?
Rheumatism: Medical conditions affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Known as rue or 'herb-of-grace,' this Mediterranean plant is prized for its bluish leaves and doubles as an insect repellent — which species?
Ruta graveolens: Species of plant. Ruta graveolens, commonly known as rue, common rue, ruda, arruda or herb-of-grace, is a species of the genus Ruta grown as an ornamental plant and herb.
This group of autoimmune diseases causes thickened skin and poor blood flow to the fingers and toes, with one form known as CREST syndrome — what is it called?
Scleroderma: Group of autoimmune diseases resulting in abnormal growth of connective tissue.
Also called herpes zoster, this viral disease paints a painful blistering rash down just one side of the body, and can leave lingering nerve pain called postherpetic neuralgia — what is it?
